reply_text:
I'll try the shared conversation and look at what generates the turns feed.㊥ (gist) The feed is fixed and republished: it now carries only your turns. I could not read the shared conversation, so if it matters, paste its text.

㊩ ("may be of interest if you can read it") The share page sits behind a Cloudflare browser check and returns only a challenge page to anything that is not a browser. Nothing of the conversation comes through.

㊬ ("showing non-operator turns") Of the 120 entries in the public feed, 97 were bells between agents, mostly claude-2's packets to codex-33, recorded with origin `agent`. The generator took the latest 120 records with no filter on origin. It now keeps operator turns only, treating records older than the origin field as operator turns. Regenerated: 120 entries, all operator, newest 01:05Z today. Commit 26ea4df98 in futon3c.

㊟ (how the feed gets refreshed) Nothing schedules the generator. The previous feed dated from 2026-10-06 and nothing had run it since, so the page will go stale again until something runs `scripts/turn_margin_html.py --latest 120 --agent all`. If you want it live, say so and I will put it on a timer.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("zai mining of Futon related scopes") I read this as the scope relation across turns, labelled over the futon missions. The pool is every unlabelled eligible operator turn stamped with a futon mission (not M-diagramprover): 208 records in five missions. Only 24 of them carry marked reply paragraphs, so this batch is mostly your own fragments (503) and their scopes. If you meant something else by scopes, say so and I'll redirect the second wave.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (batch 3) Each input now carries `mission_id` and the kernel's still-open ports at that record, so a labeller can say that a fragment sits within, or a paragraph answers, something opened in an earlier turn. The validator accepts those ids as targets. Packet, pool and harness changes are committed.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (second wave) The monthly meter was 73% used at 20:06Z and resets at 02:04Z, so what is unspent by then is lost. When these three return I'll read the window and, if it has room, send the M-diagramprover pool (114 records, the richest in reply acts) to zai-4 and zai-5, which claude-15 has finished with.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("inspired by this paper") [KnowTeX](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15294) draws theorems and proofs as a dependency graph from LaTeX with two edge sources, manual `\uses{}` and inferred rules, three edge styles, red cycles, and an edge review table where the author deletes or adds edges and exports the corrections. 象 has the same two sources over acts: the Zai-labelled incidences and the kernel's port closes. The review table is the piece we lacked: your verdicts on edges are a measurement that does not reward closing ports.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (front-end packets) codex-57 builds `graph/build_mission_graph.py`: one column per session, labelled edges beside kernel closes, agreed edges marked, Tarjan cycles red, an export of your verdicts as a JSON file whose format a later scorer reads. No graphviz on this host, so the layout is a time-layered SVG. codex-47 writes a futon6 note only: which of KnowTeX's eight rules the classical arm of `paper_hypergraph.py` already has (the default proof association and ref-in-proof visibly), measured on three golden papers, and the smallest viewer change. Jobs `invoke-1791835856732-7830-135d2c43` and `invoke-1791835860976-7831-1e38cf16`, both running.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (one slip, fixed) My first batch-3 commit went in with a failing test because the chain checked the wrong exit code. The failure was in the fixture, not the behaviour; the follow-up commit fixes it and the ten harness tests pass.
